finalText:
Here's what the log says. Everything happened in a 32-minute window, `02:00:00Z` → `02:31:52Z` on 2026-07-04.

## Timeline

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00 – 02:14 | Normal. 170 requests all `200`, cache hit ratio 0.90–0.98 |
| **02:14:07.113** | `ERROR [api] redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` |
| 02:14:07.114 | `WARN [api] cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads` |
| 02:14:03 | **Last successful request in the entire log** (`GET /orders 200 75ms`) |
| 02:14:10 | First `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` |
| 02:14:12 | Queue backlog begins: depth 52 |
| 02:15:26 – 02:31:26 | 13 redis reconnect attempts, all `ECONNREFUSED`, all from `[api]`, ~80s apart. None ever succeed |
| 02:29:12 | Queue depth crosses its own limit: `502 (max 500)` |
| 02:31:44 | `ERROR [worker-2] JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` |
| 02:31:45 | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| 02:31:52 | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

## What actually happened

Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` went away at 02:14:07 — `ECONNREFUSED`, meaning the port was actively rejecting, so the process was down or the listener gone, not a network black-hole (that would time out instead). Root cause is outside this log; you'll want the Redis host's own logs for 02:14.

The app didn't fail on that. It degraded to "direct store reads," which is the design working as intended — but the backing store couldn't absorb 100% of read traffic that the cache had been serving at a 0.9–0.98 hit ratio. So roughly 10x the read load hit it directly, and it started timing out **3 seconds later** at 02:14:10.

From there it's a textbook queue death spiral. Requests took 5000ms to fail instead of ~75ms to succeed, so arrivals outpaced completions and the backlog grew almost perfectly linearly — ~30 requests/minute, from 52 at 02:14 to 568 at 02:31. The `max 500` threshold was crossed at 02:29:12 and **nothing happened** — no shedding, no rejection, the queue just kept growing past its stated cap. That backlog is what consumed the heap: worker-2 OOM'd at 02:31:44 (exit 134 = SIGABRT, V8's OOM abort), and the supervisor killed the unresponsive api 7 seconds later.

Total counts: 348 WARN, 188 ERROR, 2 FATAL. The 174 "cache miss storm" and 173 "request queue depth" warnings are all downstream noise from the one redis failure — there is only **one** originating fault in this file.

## Two things worth flagging

**The reconnect backoff isn't backing off.** All 13 attempts are ~80 seconds apart — fixed interval, no exponential growth. Worth checking your `ioredis` `retryStrategy`; the default is exponential, so this looks like a custom override.

**The queue limit isn't enforced.** `max 500` is logged as a warning label but never acted on. This is the highest-leverage fix: with real shedding at 500, the process survives the redis outage in a degraded-but-alive state instead of OOMing. Right now a dependency being down for 17 minutes is guaranteed to take the whole service with it.

I've only read the log — I haven't looked at `src/` (it isn't in this directory) or the Redis host. Happy to dig into the retry/queue config if you can point me at the source.
